column1: # The shared boundary tests (tests/boundary.py), in this language: up and down are the script a case becomes, @V@ the value written here, @ID@ the case. A case with no v: line is one this language cannot write. @NL@ is a newline.
# The other direction (tests/boundary.py run-invoke): scripts that export subs for the host to call. x:make returns @V@; x:back hands its argument back.

column2: my $n = 0;@NL@sub count { return ++$n }@NL@sub boom { die "boom\n" }@NL@export qw(count boom);

my @pending = (txn_start("deposit"), txn_start("refund"));@NL@my $seen = 0;@NL@sub on_txn {@NL@    my ($id) = @_;@NL@    my $d = txn_details($id);@NL@    $seen++;@NL@    return "$seen $d->{kind} $d->{amount}";@NL@}@NL@export 'on_txn';
